meaning:
ζηλόω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for קָנָא pi. ;]
1. to burn with envy or jealousy, to be jealousy: absol., Act.7:9 17:5, 1Co.13:4, Jas.4:2 (R, mg., cf. Mayor, in l).
2. to seek or desire eagerly: with accusative of thing(s), 1Co.12:31 14:1 14:39 (cf. Sir.50:18, Wis.1:12); with accusative of person(s), 2Co.11:2, Gal.4:17; pass., Gal.4:18.†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: Those people are zealous for you

elsewhere.note: “The patriarchs, moved with jealousy against Joseph, sold him into Egypt. God was with him,
But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.
For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I married you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
They zealously seek you in no good way. No, they desire to alienate you, that you may seek them.
You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.
